facts.value: Capital Programme outturn £81.3m (General Fund £57.0m, HRA £24.3m) against original budget £157.2m. A £75.9m in-year underspend (48% of plan) and a £37.3m reduction from the third quarter review at £118.6m.

source.title: Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators — Year End Outturn 2025/26, Report to Cabinet 14 July 2026 (recommending to Council 16 July 2026)

facts.note: Main paper §5-6, pages 1-2. Quarterly monitoring table on p.1 shows the trajectory: £157.2m → £145.5m → £136.6m → £118.6m → £81.3m outturn. Appendix 2 (pp.7-11) gives scheme-level detail; the largest slippage items are Gateshead Flyover (£11.9m under Q3), Decent Homes HRA (£3.9m) and Transforming Cities (£2.7m).

facts.value: £81.3m funded from: Capital Grants and Contributions £28.6m; General Fund Capital Receipts £0.8m; Major Repairs Reserve (HRA) £20.9m; Right to Buy Capital Receipts (HRA) £2.3m; Capital Grants and Contributions (HRA) £1.0m; Other (Self-financing, borrowing, revenue) £27.7m.

source.title: Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators — Year End Outturn 2025/26, Report to Cabinet 14 July 2026

facts.note: Main paper §8, page 2. §7 states the use of external capital resources and capital receipts has been maximised. The £27.7m 'Other' line combines self-financing, borrowing and revenue with no split published.

facts.value: Capital Financing Requirement at 31 March 2026 (Q4 actual): Non-HRA £425.526m against a reported indicator of £477.066m (£51.5m below plan); HRA £345.505m against a reported indicator of £345.505m (exactly at plan). Total CFR £771.031m. The 2026/27 reported indicator sits at Non-HRA £460.688m + HRA £345.505m = £806.193m, and the Q1 forecast has moved Non-HRA up by £5.098m to £465.786m — Total CFR £811.291m.

source.title: Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators — Year End Outturn 2025/26, Appendix 3; and Q1 Review 2026/27 (doc 49896), Appendix 4

facts.note: Appendix 3 of the outturn paper (p.13) for 2025/26; Appendix 4 of doc 49896 for 2026/27. HRA CFR is flat at £345.505m across both years — all CFR growth is Non-HRA. The 2026/27 Q1 Non-HRA forecast moving up against the reported indicator despite a 14% capital slippage at Q1 is worth watching in the mid-year review.

facts.value: Actual external debt at 31 March 2026: £670.182m. This is also the maximum year-to-date figure recorded in both the Authorised Limit and Operational Boundary tables. No PWLB / non-PWLB split published.

source.title: Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators — Year End Outturn 2025/26, Appendix 3, page 14

facts.note: Appendix 3 states: 'The Council's actual external debt at 31 March 2026 was £670.182m. It should be noted that actual external debt is not directly comparable to the Authorised Limit and Operational Boundary, since the actual external debt reflects the position at one point in time.' No loan-by-loan detail or lender split. Not a treasury management report — treasury detail will sit in a separate paper not held in this bundle.

facts.value: £100.849m at 31 March 2026 — 13.1% of the £771.031m CFR is funded from internal balances rather than external debt.

source.title: Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators — Year End Outturn 2025/26, Appendix 3

facts.note: Derived from the paper's own figures: CFR £771.031m (Non-HRA £425.526m + HRA £345.505m) minus external borrowing £670.182m minus OLTL £0. Balance-sheet identity closes cleanly for 2025/26. For 2026/27 the identity cannot be closed from this bundle — the paper doesn't publish external borrowing at 30 June 2026 in Appendix 4 of the Q1 paper.

facts.value: Authorised Limit for External Debt: Borrowing £851m + OLTL £0 = £851m total. Operational Boundary: Borrowing £836m + OLTL £0 = £836m. Both are for 2025/26. Maximum YTD external debt against both limits was £670.182m at 31 March 2026 — leaving £165.8m of headroom under the Operational Boundary (19.8%) and £180.8m under the Authorised Limit (21.6%).

source.title: Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators — Year End Outturn 2025/26, Appendix 3, pages 13-14

facts.value: Non-HRA: 12.35% reported indicator for 2025/26; 10.76% out-turned (1.59 points below plan). HRA: 32.84% reported; 32.80% out-turned (broadly at plan). 2026/27 reported indicators are 11.37% Non-HRA and 33.47% HRA (year-end only — not reported at Q1).

source.title: Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators — Year End Outturn 2025/26, Appendix 3, page 12; Q1 Review 2026/27 (doc 49896), Appendix 4

facts.note: The Non-HRA undershoot on the ratio is consistent with Non-HRA CFR out-turning £51.5m below plan (£425.526m vs £477.066m) — less external borrowing generated less financing cost. The HRA sits at 33% financing-cost ratio — high in absolute terms; HRA CFR is flat at £345.505m across both years.

facts.value: 2026/27 original budget £165.7m (Council 26 February 2026); Q1 revised £142.29m — £23.4m below plan already at Q1. £27.094m of prior-year slippage was added and £50.548m of Q1 review movements deducted. Housing HRA down £23.454m (Decent Homes £8.978m, demolition £9.635m deferred, new build £4.222m reprofiled); City Regional Sustainable Transport Settlement down £13.355m (scope reduced to be deliverable); Gateshead Flyover up £12.289m (prior year slippage now expected to complete).

source.title: Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators — First Quarter Review 2026/27, Report to Cabinet 14 July 2026 (doc 49896)

facts.note: Q1 paper pp.1-6. Appendix 3 (5-year programme) shows the 5-year Grand Total moves from £709.827m original to £729.092m revised — the £75.9m of 2025/26 slippage and the £23.4m of 2026/27 slippage do not fall out of the plan; they move along the horizon.

facts.value: CANNOT BE CHECKED FROM THIS PAPER. The paper publishes total external debt at 31 March 2026 (£670.182m) but no PWLB / non-PWLB split, no loan-by-loan table, no maturity profile and no weighted average rate. Our ledger at 2026-03-31 for GATESHEAD BOROUGH COUNCIL holds 82 loans totalling £622,181,073 at a weighted 3.4909%; the £47.999m difference against £670.182m is plausibly non-PWLB borrowing but the paper doesn't say. Not reconcilable from the material published; per PIPELINE.md the loan-book claim is kept out of the email entirely.

source.title: Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators — Year End Outturn 2025/26, Appendix 3, page 14

facts.note: The paper is a Capital Programme monitoring report, not a treasury management report — the loan-level detail lives in a separate Treasury Management Strategy or Mid-Year Review not held in this bundle. For future reading, the next natural touchpoint is that treasury paper.

courses_named: Liability Benchmark: using it in practice
officer.body:
Dear Anna,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. More — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — is in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep both of those relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. A couple of thoughts below on the Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators report that went to Cabinet on 14 July recommending to Council on 16 July, and the Q1 review taken alongside it. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The report is clearly laid out and this is offered in that spirit, not as a critique.

The first thing that stands out on Appendix 3 is that the balance sheet closes cleanly on your own figures at 31 March 2026: Total CFR £771.031m (Non-HRA £425.526m plus HRA £345.505m), actual external debt £670.182m, Other Long Term Liabilities zero — which leaves £100.849m of the underlying need funded from internal balances, 13% of the CFR. Against an Operational Boundary of £836m you finished the year with £165.8m of headroom, and £180.8m against the Authorised Limit. Not many councils we've read carry that much external capacity — it's the shape of a council that fills more of the CFR from cash than from debt.

The second thing is what capital slippage did to the indicators. The programme out-turned at £81.3m against £157.2m budgeted — a £75.9m underspend and £37.3m below the Q3 review at £118.6m. That flowed straight through to Non-HRA CFR, which came in at £425.526m against the reported indicator of £477.066m — £51.5m below plan. And it flowed through to the financing cost ratio, which finished at 10.76% against a plan of 12.35% — 1.59 percentage points below, because less external borrowing meant less servicing cost. HRA is a different story: CFR held exactly at £345.505m against a £345.505m reported indicator, and the ratio at 32.80% almost exactly at the 32.84% plan. The Non-HRA position is where the year's arithmetic moved.

The Q1 2026/27 paper (doc 49896) has already reforecast the year down from £165.7m to £142.3m — 14% slippage booked at Q1, with the HRA down £23.5m (Decent Homes, demolition and new build all reprofiled) and CRSTS down £13.4m as the scope is reshaped to fit the funding period. Two things about that. First, Appendix 3 of that paper shows the 5-year plan grows only £19.3m against original — the slippage moves along the horizon rather than falls out, so the borrowing need is deferred not removed. Second, the Non-HRA CFR at Q1 sits £5.098m above the reported indicator (£465.786m vs £460.688m) even as delivery slips. That is directionally the opposite of what the slippage would produce on its own — worth watching in the mid-year update to see whether the underlying need has grown or whether it is the opening base resetting after the 2025/26 outturn.

We price every published PWLB book daily against the DMO's premature-repayment curve at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis. Yesterday afternoon's certainty curve was 5-year 5.34%, 10-year 5.83%, 25-year 6.46%, 50-year 6.27%, with Bank Rate at 3.75% and the OIS 1-year at 4.11%. This paper doesn't publish the loan-book detail — capital programme monitoring rather than treasury management — so we haven't run the reconciliation against your figures. If the mid-year review lands a treasury paper alongside the Q2 update, the paired view of the loan book against today's curve is the thing our tools are built for.

One standing point because CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates will put it in front of every S151: the liability benchmark pathway becomes central, with an interactive version at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity. Your ratios in Appendix 3 speak to the affordability side of the indicator set; the benchmark speaks to what has to be borrowed and when.

On training, three courses fit the paper. Balance sheet projections covers the CFR / external / internal split the outturn now fixes. Liability Benchmark: using it in practice picks up where the next paper naturally goes. Prudential Indicators: what changed sits behind the ratio movements we've picked out. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if any of it's useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Capital Programme and Prudential Indicators — Year End Outturn 2025/26 (Report to Cabinet 14 July 2026, recommending to Council 16 July 2026) at https://Gateshead.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s49893/rtc-capital-programme-and-prudential-indicators-year-end-out.pdf, taken alongside the First Quarter Review 2026/27 at https://Gateshead.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s49896/rtc-capital-programme-and-prudential-ind.pdf.
